title: Canadian benefit payment dates for December 2026 and January 2027
seoTitle: Canadian benefit payment dates: December 2026, January 2027
description: Canadian benefit payment dates for December 2026 and January 2027, including federal benefits and selected provincial programs, with official sources.
howWeChecked: Written by the flourish team, with AI tools used to help draft it. Every date was read on November 12, 2026 on the two Government of Canada pages linked above. No date here comes from a news site, a bank or social media. No financial professional reviewed this page. If a date on canada.ca differs from this page, canada.ca is right, and we would like to know: hello@flourishmoney.app.

body.html: December is the month when benefit dates move. Several payments land earlier than usual, and the first one of the new year arrives on January 5. This page lists only dates the Government of Canada has published, with the page each one came from.

All dates below were read on the Government of Canada's Benefits payment dates calendar (page dated 2026-11-12, last checked November 12, 2026). The December dates for benefits run by the Canada Revenue Agency also match the CRA's own payment dates page (page dated 2026-10-14, last checked November 12, 2026). On the day we checked, that CRA page listed 2026 dates only, so the January 2027 dates come from the calendar page alone.
Source for every row: Benefits payment dates, canada.ca, last checked November 12, 2026.
Three things stand out in December.

items: The Canada child benefit comes on the 11th. In most months of 2026 it was issued on the 20th or close to it. The gap between the December payment and the next one, on January 20, is 40 days.
Canada Pension Plan and Old Age Security come on the 22nd. In November they were issued on the 26th. The next payment after December 22 is January 27, which is 36 days later.

Three benefits on the calendar have no December payment. The calendar lists no December date for the Canada Groceries and Essentials Benefit, the Advanced Canada workers benefit or the Alberta child and family benefit.

body.html: Source for every row: Benefits payment dates, canada.ca, last checked November 12, 2026.

Not published yet: on the day we checked, the calendar listed veteran disability pension dates for 2026 only. No January 2027 date was there, so none is listed here. The Alberta child and family benefit has no January date; its next one on the calendar is February 26, 2027.

body.text: About the Canada Groceries and Essentials Benefit

body.html: This is the quarterly payment for people and families with low and modest incomes. It took its current name in July 2026, and the CRA says the eligibility rules are the same as before (CRA, last checked November 12, 2026). The calendar lists four dates for 2027: January 5, April 5, July 5 and October 5. Related provincial and territorial programs are included with the same payment.

The calendar page is plain about this: payments are issued on the dates listed but may take a few days to arrive, and a mailed cheque may take longer than direct deposit. It asks people to wait 5 to 10 business days before contacting the program (canada.ca, last checked November 12, 2026).

The CRA gives a number for each of its benefits: wait 5 working days from the payment date for the Canada child benefit and the Alberta child and family benefit, and 10 working days for the others it runs (CRA, last checked November 12, 2026).
Two more things from those pages:

items: The CRA offers reminders about one week before a payment is issued, and My Account shows your next payment.
The calendar page carries a warning about false information online. The CRA says its email notifications will not ask for personal information or ask you to click a link.
Amounts. What you receive depends on your own file. Your CRA account and My Service Canada Account show your figures.
Provincial programs that are not on the federal calendar. Check your province's own site.
Employment Insurance, which is not on the calendar page.

body.text: Putting the dates next to your bills

body.html: The reason to care about a date moving is what sits around it. A child benefit that arrives on December 11 and again on January 20 leaves a long stretch with rent or a mortgage payment, a phone bill and the holidays inside it.
A paper calendar can show this too. Benefit payment dates and bill due dates on the same calendar make the gaps easier to see.
